title: Tamsin and the Harbor Revisited
premise: Vesper Nystrom built his career orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly dismantling his own capacity for love, so when a snowstorm traps him at a coastal inn with Ilse Marchetti — the rival planner he betrayed a decade ago, and the woman he walked away from — old wounds and older desires resurface. Ilse has returned to the harbor town not for him but to expose how he once stole the festival contract that saved his business and ruined hers, and her evidence sits in a folder she keeps almost within his reach. As the storm isolates them and the town's winter festival becomes their shared project, Vesper must choose between confessing the theft that built his life or letting Ilse leave on the last train with her truth and his silence. He confesses — publicly, at the festival's closing night — and Ilse, who came for revenge and stayed for the man beneath it, chooses to stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: Tamsin Eastwick spent five years coordinating weddings in harbor towns before trading seating charts for sentences, and she still cries at vows she writes herself. She lives on a cold coast with a warm dog and a firm belief that every heart is trainable, given the right instructor.

chapters.title: The Last Train Before the Storm
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Arriving in Harrow Bay to plan the winter festival's closing gala, Vesper discovers his rival for the contract is Ilse Marchetti, the woman he loved and abandoned ten years ago after secretly sabotaging her bid for the same festival. A snowstorm seals the roads and strands them both at the Harbor Rest Inn. The beat: dread laced with longing — proximity as threat.

chapters.title: What the Folder Knows
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Trapped together, they're forced into uneasy collaboration when the inn's generator fails and the festival committee begs both planners to salvage the event. Ilse works by day and interrogates by night, her folder of evidence — proof of Vesper's decade-old theft — hidden in her room. The beat: wary intimacy; she wants the truth and, dangerously, him.

chapters.title: Snowlight and Confessions
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. During the festival's opening night, a power outage leaves them alone among candlelit stalls, and Ilse confronts him with the folder. Vesper admits the sabotage but begs her to wait one day — let the festival succeed, then ruin him. She agrees, and the truce cracks into a night of honesty and rekindled desire. The beat: the heart, untrainable after all.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the closing gala, Vesper confesses the theft publicly to the committee, surrendering the contract and his reputation. Ilse, who boarded the platform intending to leave, watches him choose truth over survival — the thing he never taught himself to do — and steps back off the train. The beat: resolution; loyalty to truth wins, and someone stays.
